cases.proves_bugs: BUG-711 (typed spot-level input: a number in metres with an optional P or m is accepted and written as P plus 3 decimals; "18600" is refused and asked again; read back from the placed blocks' LEVEL attributes). BUG-711's "RL" and comma examples are recorded, not judged.
cases.title: CDSL writes 18.6m, P18.6 and 18.600 as the level P18.600, refuses 18600 and asks again, and Esc then places nothing
cases.plan_item: Spot level typed input (triage group V2; daily card D26, the typed-level half); BUG-711
cases.reviewed_against: builder-filled: Opus review still needed. Compared by the builder on 25 Oct 2026 with BUG-711 in BUG_CARPARK.md (expected: a number in metres, optional P or RL, is accepted; bad input is asked again; the text is written as P plus 3 dp) and daily card D26 step 5 ("18600" refusal wording). Not claimed: BUG-713 to BUG-716 (the spot-level finder, CDSLAB and the pit design-level offer are not driven) and the survey half of D26.
cases.expected: CDSL at three points with the levels 18.6m, P18.6 and 18.600 prints "Spot level placed. Level: P18.600" three times and the three placed SPOT LEVEL blocks (layer 25DIMS) each hold the attribute value P18.600 (never PP18.6 and never P18.6m). CDSL with 18600 prints the refusal sentence and asks again; Esc then prints "CDSL command cancelled. Nothing was placed." and the block count stays at three. The drawing file is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The typed answer, the refusal loop and the attribute written into the real SPOT LEVEL block only meet in a live CDSL run.
not_automated: "RL18.6" and "18,6" are typed once each and recorded; their result is not judged (the bug entry names them but the card does not say what is right).
BUG-713 (the spot-level finder ignoring blank blocks), BUG-714 (CDSLAB versus the finder), BUG-715, BUG-716 and the existing-survey-level line of D26 are NOT driven.
